Video Title: 66 Friday Sermon 10 Dec. 1982 By Dr Rashad Khalifa
Text: A man: ...(Allahu) Akbar.
Speaker: A man
Description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa delivers a Friday sermon in Tucson, Arizona, explaining the purpose of human creation and the command to worship God alone as stated in Sura 67:1-2. He shows a slide of Earth from space to emphasize cosmic scale and human insignificance, arguing that venerated figures such as Jesus, Abraham, and Muhammad were temporary earthly residents. Citing Suras 5:75, 21:8, and 25:7, 20, he notes that prophets required food and visited markets, critiquing Hadith regulations regarding ritual purity and hygiene. He references Sura 24:55 to affirm that monotheists receive earthly authority, sharing an account of a woman surviving a gunshot to the head to illustrate God's ultimate sovereignty over life and death. In the second sermon, he discusses letters from a supporter in India who abandoned Hadith, claims Egyptian contractor Uthman Ahmad Uthman published one million copies of his Arabic booklet, and announces post-Zikr Arabic classes. He addresses converts maintaining their birth names rather than adopting Arabic ones, recounting an Iranian girl named Sherry who felt alienated by Arabic names at the mosque, which prompts a debate with attendees over slave names and adoption rules. Following congregational prayer, Dean Mahmoud recites Sura 2:168-176 and critiques extra-Quranic food restrictions, including Hanafi bans on shellfish, Indian cow veneration, Southeast Asian Hadiths against cucumbers, and Chinese ancestor offerings. Khalifa concludes by outlining the four explicit Quranic food prohibitions, dismissing Hadith bans on footwear and soap ingredients, and answering questions on store-bought meat and blood sausages before attendees recite Sura 2:177 and 2:178-179.
